Why you are seeing this early

Before the signboard, before the portals.

The owners have asked to show the home quietly first, to buyers already looking in Beenleigh, before it is advertised to the whole market.

That is worth something to you. You get to walk through it without a crowd, take your time, ask everything, and make a decision before it is in front of thousands of people on a portal.

The window is ten days and it closes after the viewing on Saturday 10 October. If a buyer and the owners agree on terms before then, the home sells here and never goes public at all. If not, it is advertised openly the following week — portals, signboard, open homes, and every buyer in Logan looking at it on the same morning.

So the honest position is this: for ten days you are competing with almost nobody. After that you are competing with everybody.

Why this one

What you would have to build to get this anywhere else.

There are other three-bedroom houses in Beenleigh. There are not many with this much already done to them, and that is the whole argument for this one.

  • The outdoor half is builtA hundred and fourteen square metres of covered outdoor room across the patio and the Bali hut, a finished studio, a fire pit, and stone retaining walls and staircases front and back. Adding that to a plain brick-and-tile house is years of work and a serious bill. Here it is finished, planted and grown in.
  • Nothing needs money spent on itKitchen, bathroom, laundry, internal doors, paint, roof, security screens, alarm, cameras, solar, three split systems, new garage door, smoke alarm compliance. It is a long, dull list, and every item on it is already done.
  • It houses two households without a conversionThe studio is a separate room with a door you can shut, at the bottom of the garden rather than off the hallway. A teenager, a parent, a business, a studio — without touching the house or applying for anything.
  • One owner, thirty-seven yearsMaintained by people who were staying, not dressed up by somebody who was leaving. The difference shows in the parts of a house nobody photographs.
  • A cul-de-sac, in a school catchment617 square metres on a street with no through traffic, inside the Beenleigh State School catchment. You can renovate a kitchen. You cannot renovate your way to a quiet street.

The house

Renovated by the only family who has ever lived in it.

It was bought new in 1989 and has never been sold. Everything that has been done to it since was done by people who intended to stay — which is a different standard from a renovation done to sell.

The kitchen has stone benchtops with matching stone splashbacks, Bosch appliances, and under-cabinet strip lighting on a remote. The laundry was done in the same stone.

The bathroom and toilet are tiled floor to ceiling, with a large deep soaking bath, a toilet with a built-in bidet, and German Hansgrohe tapware. Every internal door and handle is new, the interior has been freshly painted, and there are LED downlights through the main living area and kitchen.

  • KitchenStone benchtops and splashbacks, Bosch appliances, remote-controlled under-cabinet strip lighting
  • BathroomFloor-to-ceiling tiles, large deep soaking bath, toilet with built-in bidet, Hansgrohe German tapware
  • LaundryRenovated, with stone benchtops and splashbacks to match the kitchen
  • BedroomsThree, with three large built-in wardrobes
  • Flexible livingA main living area large enough to double as an additional sleeping space
  • FinishesNew internal doors and handles, fresh interior paint, LED downlights to living and kitchen
  • StorageThree large wardrobes inside, plus a garden shed outside

Outside

Most of this house is not inside it.

Seventy-eight square metres of covered patio runs the back of the house — thirteen metres by six. Not a pergola over a slab: a proper covered room without walls, big enough for a long table and everyone around it. It is the reason the first viewing is at twilight.

Beyond it, another thirty-six square metres under the Bali hut, set up for a spa or a barbecue, a dedicated fire pit area, and a flat grass zone for kids and a dog. Stone retaining walls and staircases front and back. The garden is landscaped and deliberately low maintenance — no large trees to deal with.

That is a hundred and fourteen square metres of covered outdoor room before you count the studio — more floor area than a lot of two-bedroom units, and none of it needs air conditioning.

Two side entries mean you can get a trailer, a mower or a wheelbarrow to the back without going through the house.

78 m²Covered patioThirteen metres by six, under roof.

The studio

A separate room at the bottom of the garden.

Ten square metres — two and a half by four — detached from the house and fully fitted out — power points, lighting, and carpet laid over underlay. It is finished, not a shell.

Which is the point: a home office with a door you can shut, a teenage retreat, a yoga studio, a media room, a guest room, or somewhere for a parent to stay. Most houses at this end of the market do not have a second, separate space at all.

Together with the patio and the Bali hut, it is what lets this house work for two households as easily as one. It is an outbuilding, not a self-contained flat — there is no kitchen or bathroom in it.

Where it is

A court, which is the quiet kind of street.

Viewbank Court is a cul-de-sac, so the only traffic on it is people who live there. If you have small children or a dog, that is not a small thing.

The home sits inside the Beenleigh State School catchment for Prep to Year 6, and Beenleigh's shops, train station and services are a few minutes away. The M1 is close enough to commute north to Brisbane or south to the Gold Coast without living on top of it.

Two houses in this street have sold in the last six months, so there is recent, local evidence of what buyers think of the address.
